Review date: 2026-08-04. Package version reviewed: TaxaAssign 0.1.0. Review conducted by
Claude Code, using the template in `inst/Code and Domain Review 2.Rmd`. This is TaxaAssign's
first full review of this kind -- every sibling package in the ecosystem that has one
(TaxaTools, TaxaFetch, TaxaMatch, TaxaLikely, TaxaExpect) already had one; this closes that
gap. Findings and fixes are combined in one pass (no separate response document), following
the `taxafetch_review.Rmd`/`taxaexpect_review.Rmd` precedent: every R file (19 source files,
~9,300 lines) was read in full against the template's five criteria, candidate findings were
verified directly against the source (not inferred), and every fix applied was re-verified by
re-running the full test suite and `R CMD check` afterward.

`devtools::test()`: 615 expectations, 0 failures (unchanged from before this review -- these
fixes are style/consistency/documentation, not behavior, and no test asserted on the exact
wording of any message this review touched beyond the substrings preserved below). 13
pre-existing warnings (informational messages the test suite deliberately captures) and 1 skip
(TaxaTools-not-installed path, environment-dependent), both unchanged. `devtools::check()`:
0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes. Reinstalled to `~/Library/R/4.0/library`.

# Code Review

Purpose: To produce high quality code that is well written and organized according to
best coding practices.

### [x] Functionality: The code is readable, organized, and efficient.

TaxaAssign is a mature package (19 R source files, extensively documented, 615 passing
tests) that has already been through many rounds of ecosystem-wide correctness fixes --
see `CLAUDE.md`'s ~40 dated session notes. No functionality bugs were found this session;
the code is readable and consistently organized (roxygen throughout, `.`-prefixed
`@noRd` internal helpers, `package::function()` cross-package calls, shared helpers
factored into `.run_consensus_and_report()`/`site_utils.R`). The findings below are
style, consistency, and DRY issues, plus one latent packaging bug surfaced by a newer
local `roxygen2` version -- none change any function's behavior.

### [x] Optimizations: no inefficiencies found; two DRY violations fixed.

**Base R `stop()`/`warning()`/`message()` used inconsistently with the package's own `cli`
convention (fixed).** `DESCRIPTION` declares `cli` as a formal `Imports`, and 14 of 19 R
files use `cli::cli_abort()`/`cli_warn()`/`cli_inform()` exclusively or predominantly for
user-facing messages. Five files used base `stop()`/`warning()`/`message()` exclusively
instead: `site_utils.R` (10 calls), `run_bayesian_pipeline.R` (7), `build_context.R` (7),
`group_priors.R` (5), `report_assign.R` (2) -- plus a handful of stray base calls scattered
inside otherwise-`cli` files (`compute_posterior.R`, `posterior_consensus.R` x2,
`join_priors.R`, `slash_taxon.R`). Most strikingly, `run_bayesian_pipeline.R` and
`run_llm_pipeline.R` are sibling entry points with the identical `backbone_id` validation
check, but one used `stop()` and the other `cli::cli_abort()` for the exact same error.
**Fixed:** all 31 base calls across these files converted to the equivalent `cli::`
call, preserving every substring an existing test regex checks (verified by reading
every `expect_error()`/`expect_warning()` in the affected test files before editing, not
after). The two identical `.msg <- function(...) if (verbose) message(...)` progress-message
wrappers in `run_bayesian_pipeline.R`/`run_llm_pipeline.R` were deliberately left as-is --
they're a consistent, shared, `verbose`-gated convention between the two sibling pipeline
functions, not a stray inconsistency.

**Triplicated LLM-prompt context-block logic (fixed).** `assign_taxa_llm.R`'s
`.build_taxa_prompt()` and `suggest_unreferenced_species.R`'s `.build_plausible_prompt()`
and `.build_family_prompt()` each independently built an identical ~15-line "Context:\n..."
block from a `ctx` list (same field list, same label-lookup `switch()`, same
`nzchar(trimws(...))` filtering), differing only in which field name holds the habitat
value (`"main_habitat"` vs `"habitat"`). Extracted to a single shared helper,
`.build_context_block(ctx, habitat_field)`, in `site_utils.R` (this package's existing
home for small cross-file internal helpers); all three call sites now call it directly.
Verified line-by-line equivalent to the three original blocks before replacing them.

### [x] Coding standards: one base-R name collision fixed; documentation is thorough and (with one packaging fix) builds cleanly.

**`rtruncnorm_at_zero(n, mean, sd)` shadowed `base::mean` and `stats::sd` as parameter
names (fixed).** `compute_posterior.R`'s internal truncated-normal sampler used `mean`
and `sd` as its own parameter names -- exactly the class of collision the review template
calls out by name. Not an active bug (the function body never calls `mean()`/`sd()`
internally, so nothing was silently shadowed at runtime), but poor practice per tidyverse
naming guidance and a real readability hazard if the function is ever extended to call
either generic. Renamed to `mu`/`sigma` (the conventional statistical notation for a
normal distribution's parameters, and unambiguous). The function is called positionally
at its one call site, so this is a pure internal rename with no behavior change.

No other base-R/`stats`-shadowing object names were found (`grep`-checked the whole `R/`
directory for bare `df`/`data`/`T`/`F`/`c`/`mean`/`sd`/`var`/`range`/`filter`/`format`/
`table`/`sum`/`length`/`unique`/`sort`/`order`/`levels` assignments; the only hits were
this one and unrelated `format = ...` named arguments to `cli::cli_progress_bar()`, which
is the function's own real parameter name, not a collision).

**Latent packaging bug: 4 multi-line `@importFrom` roxygen blocks (fixed).**
`assign_taxa_llm.R` (x2), `join_priors.R`, and `suggest_unreferenced_species.R` each had a
single `@importFrom pkg fn1 fn2 ...` tag wrapped onto a second line
(`#'   fn3 fn4 ...`). This was tolerated by older `roxygen2` but is a hard error under the
locally installed `roxygen2` 8.0.0 (`"@importFrom must be only 1 line long, not 2"`),
which silently aborted `devtools::document()` partway through and left those four files'
`NAMESPACE`/`.Rd` entries stale on this machine. Not something this review's edits
introduced -- these blocks predate this session -- but it blocks a clean `document()` run
for anyone documenting this package with a current `roxygen2`, which the
"Automated tests: confirm all tests pass" checklist item below depends on. Fixed by
splitting each into two single-line `@importFrom` tags for the same package (e.g.
`@importFrom dplyr filter arrange desc group_by ungroup left_join` /
`@importFrom dplyr bind_rows slice_max n_distinct summarise`) -- semantically identical,
just reformatted. `devtools::document()` now completes with no errors; `DESCRIPTION`'s
`RoxygenNote`/`Config/roxygen2/version` fields were updated by `document()` to reflect
this.

Docstrings are present and thorough for every exported function (often with dedicated
`@details`/`@section` blocks explaining *why*, not just *what* -- e.g.
`update_prior_from_consensus()`'s "Confirmation-quantile design" section walks through
several rejected alternatives and why each failed). In-line comments are informative and,
where checked against the code they describe, accurate (see the Comment accuracy note
below for the one place this needed a closer look).

**Minor, not fixed (per the template's "minor violations can be ignored or briefly
mentioned" guidance):** roxygen `@param` blocks in several files use manually
column-aligned `=` signs with inconsistent column widths across nearby lines (e.g.
`assign_taxa_llm()`'s own signature block, `R/assign_taxa_llm.R:284-310`) -- cosmetic
only, doesn't affect parsing or readability materially, and "fixing" alignment across a
whole file risks noisy diffs for zero functional benefit. `NEWS.md` documents only
"Sessions 57-59" and predates the dozens of subsequent sessions recorded in `CLAUDE.md`
-- a real but low-priority documentation gap (this package's session history is the
authoritative record; `NEWS.md` was not kept in sync), left as-is since backfilling ~40
sessions' worth of user-facing changelog entries is a substantial undertaking outside
this review's scope, not a quick fix.

### [x] Automated tests: all pass.

`devtools::test()`: 615/615 passing both before and after this review's edits (13
pre-existing informational warnings, 1 pre-existing environment-dependent skip, both
unchanged). `devtools::check()`: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes (after the `@importFrom`
fix above -- see that finding for why `check()`/`document()` would otherwise fail on a
current `roxygen2` installation).

### [x] Vulnerabilities: none found.

TaxaAssign does no direct file-system, network, or shell access of its own -- it consumes
already-fetched data frames (`match_df`, `taxaexpect_priors`) and delegates LLM calls to a
caller-supplied `llm_fn`. The one place user-controlled text reaches an external system is
`assign_taxa_llm()`/`suggest_unreferenced_species()`/`build_context()` building free-text
LLM prompts from taxon names and context strings -- these are interpolated into prompt text
via `paste0()`/`sprintf()`, not into a shell command, SQL query, or file path, so this is a
prompt-injection-shaped surface (a taxon name with adversarial content could try to
influence the LLM's response) rather than a code-execution one, and is inherent to any
LLM-prompting function, not specific to this package. `.parse_taxa_response()`/
`.parse_plausible_response()`/`.parse_family_response()` all wrap `jsonlite::fromJSON()` in
`tryCatch()` and validate the parsed shape before use, so a malformed or adversarial LLM
response degrades to a documented uniform-prior/empty-list fallback rather than crashing or
executing anything.

Any additional comments, list below in comment section.

No further comments.

# Domain Review

Purpose: To ensure the code produces outputs, data, interfaces, or software that is
biologically reasonable when compared to other similar information available. Review
should be conducted by someone with applicable subject-matter knowledge.

### [x] Scientific Rigor

TaxaAssign's Bayesian machinery (`compute_posterior()`'s truncated-normal likelihood
sampling and Beta-distributed prior sampling, `posterior_consensus()`'s LCA-based
consensus, `update_prior_from_consensus()`'s confirmation-quantile empirical Bayes step)
has already been the subject of extensive, dated statistical soundness review recorded in
`CLAUDE.md` and `ecosystem_docs/STATISTICAL_COMPONENT_SOUNDNESS_REVIEW.md` -- including
several real derivation corrections (e.g. the 2026-07-09 truncated-normal fix removing a
spurious point mass at 0; the 2026-07-30 `consensus_prior` redesign from a
candidate-scoped MAX to a group-level SUM, justified by finite additivity of a
compositional share). This review did not re-derive that work; no new statistical claim
in the package's documentation was found unsubstantiated, and every formula checked
against its roxygen description matched (e.g. `combine_multisite_priors()`'s
precision-weighted logit combination correctly implements the stated
`digamma`/`trigamma` exact-moment formulas for a Beta-distributed logit transform).

### [x] Outputs

No units/constants (e.g. "density of granite"-style physical constants) apply to this
package -- its numeric outputs are probabilities and Beta-distribution parameters, whose
correctness was assessed under Scientific Rigor above. Output columns are documented with
their exact scale and interpretation (e.g. `posterior_consensus()`'s extensive `@return`
block distinguishes `winner_prior` from the newer `winner_theta_mean`, explicitly warning
that the two are NOT interchangeable and why -- `winner_prior` can be inflated by the
empirical Bayes confirmation boost while `winner_theta_mean` cannot, by construction).

### [x] Algorithms

The LCA (lowest common ancestor) consensus algorithm, dark-diversity hierarchical prior
fallback, and empirical Bayes confirmation-quantile refinement are all standard,
appropriate techniques for this problem and are used correctly where checked. One
existing design point is worth restating here since it is exactly the kind of thing this
checklist item asks to verify and not assume: `score_consensus()` deliberately
reproduces a conventional fixed-percent-identity-threshold pipeline (GITA/Jonah
Ventures-style) so its output can be compared against TaxaAssign's own Bayesian pathway
on the same data -- its well-documented inability to reliably separate a species from its
closest congener at typical thresholds is not a defect in this function, confirmed
directly in its own `@section Purpose` and cross-checked against
`diagnostics/score_floor_roc_sweep.R`'s real ROC-style validation cited there. No
algorithmic flaws were found.

### Comment accuracy check

One place deserved a closer look because it's easy to misread on a fast pass:
`.merge_llm_priors()` (`R/assign_taxa_llm.R`) sets `merged$prior_source[[i]] <-
"na_fill_fallback"` inside a loop guarded by `if (is.na(merged$prior_source[[i]]))` --
this reads at first glance like it could reference a column that was never created for
the `unk_idx` (unreferenced-family) rows earlier in the same function. Traced the full
data flow: `prior_source` always exists by this point because it comes from
`.parse_taxa_response()`'s output (`prior_df`), which unconditionally includes a
`prior_source` column (`"llm"` or `"uniform_fallback"`) for every named taxon; the
`unk_idx` rows (NA `taxon_name`) never match anything in the `left_join()` and so
correctly get `NA` there, which is exactly what this later loop's `is.na()` guard is
checking for. No bug -- the comment/code both hold up under tracing, included here only
because verifying it took a genuine trace rather than a glance, and a future reader might
have the same "wait, does this column exist?" reaction.
